title: INT8: slim quantization profile integration and cross-variant drift exercise
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Integrate newly-derived slim INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ/AWQ variants) into the nightly regression pipeline, validate fidelity across model variants, and run a cross-variant drift exercise to surface stability regressions. Goal: ensure embeddings and generative outputs remain within acceptable fidelity budgets while verifying fallback and canary routing behaviors under synthetic load.
acceptance_criteria: Slim INT8 profiles are ingested into the profile registry and surfaced to the canary runner
Nightly regression includes golden answer delta checks (embedding cosine, logprob delta, token-level perplexity) against golden set
Canary mesh exercise runs for 24h with simulated cross-variant traffic and reports <1% high-severity fidelity regressions
Rollback playbook executed successfully in staging with model fallback to FP16 variant and no increased error rate observed
Telemetry dashboards show stable token cost reductions and no unbounded latency increases during batched runs
testing_plan: Create a 3k-example golden prompt set derived from multilingal in-house evals and customer anonymized traces
Shadow deploy GPTQ and AWQ profile variants via canary mesh; use 50/50 traffic split in staging
Run adversarial jitter test: randomize sequence lengths (8-2048) and inject 2% malformed tokens to test stability
Capture metrics: embedding cosine similarity, answer logprob delta, token-level latency P95, memory delta, and top-k token distribution shift
Nightly regression runs: run profile ingest -> calibration replay -> output diff -> alert if >0.8% of prompts exceed thresholds
decisions: Use slim profiles (reduced per-layer metadata) to speed ingestion and lower storage overhead; accepted small increase in calibration variance in exchange for faster canary churn
Favor embedding cosine + answer-level logprob delta as primary fidelity signals rather than single NLG metrics (ROUGE/BLEU) to capture both retrieval and generation behavior
Leverage existing calibration-replay harness from ENG-211998 and extend to record kv-cache warmup patterns
Implement progressive rollback: primary fallback to FP16 model, secondary fallback to model variant with conservative quant params
Do not gate rollout on synthetic latency-only tests; require fidelity checks to pass before promoted rollout
